top_choice_rationale: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the clearest case of a simple, general mechanism (a small twist producing a moire superlattice with nearly flat bands) that gave a quantitative prediction (Bistritzer-MacDonald) followed by an experiment (Jarillo-Herrero) that found correlated insulators and superconductivity, since reproduced by many independent groups. The citation can be confined to the flat-band prediction and the observed phases, leaving the pairing mechanism aside. Maturity and the omission of Cao and others are real weaknesses, but the three-name allocation follows the conceptual origin plus the decisive experiment. Optical lattice clocks (P001) are a mature, defensible second choice, though nearer a refinement of a line honoured in 2005 and 2012; IceCube (P003) is a secure diffuse-flux discovery with unsettled attribution (Spiering); no award is worse than any of these.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Mehlig is in the same Gothenburg physics environment as Johansson and Olsson, but has no apparent connection to any candidate on the slate
